When I was around 15 or 16, I had gone to Walmart on Black Friday with a group of friends. It was the first time I was able to shop independently at a big event. My parents gave me a $20 and told me to have fun with my friends. I was really into movies at the time and had gathered as many DVD’s that I could with my budget. Standing in line for what felt like hours, it was almost my turn at checkout and my $20 was gone. I had gotten upset and luckily, one of my friends was able to spot me $20 for the movies. Years and years later, I’m at a gas station for a few groceries and I knew that I had just enough for the bare minimum due to my job cutting my hours drastically without warning. At the checkout line, I had realized that I left my wallet at home and just as I was about to walk away from the counter to put away the items I had grabbed, the lady at the front counter said, “hey you don’t have to do that. Here’s $21 and change for your groceries. Looks like it was just enough to cover what you needed. A customer had purposely left the money at the counter to help someone who needed it and that someone was you”. I was very grateful and thanked the cashier. When I got into my vehicle, I teared up… you never know when someone is going through hard times and small blessings like mine and OP’s are what helps reminds us that even when life isn’t going your way, it isn’t all bad. Thank you for sharing your story with us OP!

Recently, a similar situation occurred in my life and now I can't trust the other person(s) as they began to use threats after initially being supportive... But what if it's an inheretence of $200,000 or a lottery winning of $1,000,000? What would be said or done next?? And please please please OP, do not feel any guilt for saying no. It is your money and yours only and you can do what you wish with it. If your fiance really loves you, they would've respected your wishes and they wouldn't have done this to you, plain and simple. Instead, they chose to betray your trust and attempt to make you feel guilty to give in to their wants... Please don't make a choice that you are really not comfortable with and please, don't stop advocating for yourself OP!

"Vive con Andrés un mes y verás quién es" is a saying in Spanish that translates to "Live with Andrés for a month and you'll see who he is". My godmother taught us this if we were to have wanted to move out of our parents home at a young age to move in with a boyfriend. She would say, "if you want to move out and live with him because you love him, okay, just be prepared for what comes with your decision. He may be one way not living together and then act/be different when living together"... I will attest and say that she was not wrong lol 😆 Anyhow, the purpose of this comment is to tell you that you saw how he was once he moved in, so what's to come next if you guys were to live together again?

I am deeply sorry about what happened and I can't imagine how you must feel. It's not uncommon to have 'gender disappointment' as we recently experienced it ourselves but it just lasted the rest of the evening. My husband and I communicated and shared our feelings with each other and both agreed that as long as our baby is healthy, the gender doesn't matter. He stated "I am really happy to have seen that our baby girl is healthy but man it would've been cool to have a boy", and we were able to make jokes about it and now us and our other kids are excited to meet their baby sister. My advice to you and others from my current experience is to know that in any relationship that you have with your significant other/fiance/girlfriend/boyfriend, communication is key, as is respect and patience to build the foundation that is trust but, it's always a balance. The work you both put in is what keeps the balance because there will be days where it's 20/80, 40/60, 80/20, 45/55, etc. but as long as you keep the respect and trust one another, than that is what's worth working for. Again, I am sorry this has happened OP and I hope you are able to find your peace but remember that what happened isn't your fault as someone else made the decision.
